A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEUBAY research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–I. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit experiments, evaluations across 33 D4RL and NeoRL datasets, ablations, model-error analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Bayesian objective, normalized world-model ensemble, adaptive rollout truncation, and recurrent actor–critic procedure are retained. v2 explicitly describes fixing one model per rollout, which was already specified by v1's Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same bandit scenarios and 33 datasets covering D4RL locomotion, Adroit, AntMaze, and NeoRL locomotion. The additional model-error evaluation scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1 and 10–12, including the two MOBILE variants in AntMaze. Newly discussed methods such as ADM-v2 and Infoprop are related-work additions, without new benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Data splits, normalization, evaluation episodes, training budgets, model configurations, and hyperparameter sweeps are unchanged. Appendix G reorganizes existing settings, retaining the 1,000-transition held-out validation set and ensemble-selection procedure.

E4.justification: The same horizon, ensemble-size, uncertainty-penalty, memory, learning-rate, and data-ratio analyses remain. LayerNorm error studies and AntMaze failure cases are retained. Appendices H.2 and H.3 exchange positions without adding analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain six-seed benchmark reporting, standard deviations, Welch's one-sided t-tests at p < 0.05, and the existing rollout percentile summaries. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding tables retain identical values, including NEUBAY's locomotion averages of 80.1 on D4RL and 64.7 on NeoRL. All embedded plots and images are identical; their relocation introduces no new results or changed trends.

T1.justification: The LayerNorm bound, Bellman-error derivation, concentrability definitions, propositions, Theorem 1, and proofs are retained. Equations 5–6 exchange numbering, while Appendix C.2 changes explanatory prose without revising its assumptions or derivation.

C1.justification: The non-conservative Bayesian contribution, claimed benchmark achievements, and advantage of long horizons remain. v2 foregrounds long horizons' role in reducing overestimation, already explicitly claimed in v1's introduction and experimental discussion.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 now explicitly distinguishes its sign-agnostic error bound from an explanation of optimistic critic errors through extrapolation and shared parameters. Appendix A clarifies adaptation without parameter updates and discusses how conservatism affects the usefulness of full versus adaptive horizons.

D1.justification: Architecture, initialization, training and planning details, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, and code/checkpoint disclosures are retained. The expanded organization of Appendix G consolidates information already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for ADM-v2, Infoprop, in-context RL, and offline-to-online learning, including a new concurrent-work subsection. It removes the Gustafsson et al. citation. These refine positioning while retaining the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: The central method narrative is substantially reorganized around why long horizons are needed, how rollouts work, world-model architecture, and recurrent training. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are revised accordingly; ensemble background moves to Section 2, and experimental and appendix discussions are reordered.

P2.justification: Figures 2, 4, and 5 and the algorithm boxes are relocated. Appendix horizon and compounding-error figure groups exchange order and are renumbered. Plot content and table structures remain unchanged, with limited caption formatting and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the central long-horizon argument easier to follow and more carefully explains the relationship between the unchanged error bound and overestimation. Added concurrent-work and adaptation discussions improve context and scope clarity. These are useful but limited gains; the method, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
